metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton said he was pushing to start on intermediate tyres before the choice of a slick compound led to a disastrous beginning to the Bahrain Grand Prix for Ferrari.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver reveals debate that preceded disastrous tyre choice at start of Bahrain GP in Malaysia | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver reveals debate that preceded disastrous tyre choice at start of Bahrain GP in Malaysia Lewis Hamilton dropped from second on the grid to near the rear of the field after Ferrari opted to start on slick tyres in wet conditions at the start of the Bahrain Grand Prix; Hamilton fought back to claim a podium amid further strategy debate during the race Sunday 4 October 2026 15:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reveals his heart sank when Ferrari chose to start on soft tyres while the majority of other cars started on intermediates Lewis Hamilton said he was pushing to start on intermediate tyres before the choice of a slick compound led to a disastrous beginning to the Bahrain Grand Prix for Ferrari. Hamilton had qualified second on the grid at the Sepang International Circuit - with Malaysia hosting the race amid ongoing conflict in the Middle East - but his hopes of victory were blown as Ferrari chose to start both him and team-mate Charles Leclerc on soft slick tyres in the hope that the wet track would quickly dry out once the cars took to it. metadata.content: ParisLongchamp: Amusingly triumphs in Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere clash with Folsom Blues | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content ParisLongchamp: Amusingly triumphs in Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere clash with Folsom Blues The supplemented Amusingly showed her quality when defeating the well-fancied Folsom Blues and Avec Toi in the Qatar Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere on Arc day; Also, Green Empress provided Joseph O'Brien with top honours in the Prix Marcel Boussac. Sunday 4 October 2026 14:06, UK Image: Amusingly wins the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere (Cal Sport Media via AP Images) Amusingly oozed class in beating the colts to land the Qatar Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere at ParisLongchamp. Francis-Henri Graffard surprised many when switching his Juddmonte-owned filly from the Prix Marcel Boussac against her own sex, but the decision was well and truly vindicated. Colin Keane dropped his mount out last in the early stages and she tracked the odds-on favourite Folsom Blues, with both travelling ominously well. Joseph O'Brien's National Stakes winner had no answer to the finishing burst of Amusingly, though, and the daughter of No Nay Never pulled away to win in tremendous fashion. Graffard said: "She beat the filly that finished second in the Marcel Boussac (Data) very easily, so I was hoping I didn't make a mistake. messages.text: FIA explain 'unprecedented' glitch that caused Bahrain GP start chaos

metadata.summary: The FIA revealed an “unprecedented” glitch caused several cars to stop in the chaotic start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
metadata.content: FIA explain 'unprecedented' glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia start chaos on formation laps | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content FIA explain 'unprecedented' glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia start chaos on formation laps The formation laps at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia saw several drivers slowing to a crawl or stopping completely; watch the Singapore GP Sprint weekend from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 4 October 2026 15:18, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit The FIA revealed an “unprecedented” glitch caused several cars to stop in the chaotic start to the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. Heavy rain in Sepang caused a delayed start but when the drivers left the pit lane, multiple drivers almost grinded to a halt including race leader Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton with several drivers in the midfield also experiencing issues. The start procedure was abandoned and the Grand Prix eventually started properly with the original grid order almost an hour after the carnage. messages.text: Roosters hold on to break Newcastle hearts in NRL Grand Final

metadata.summary: Hull FC-bound Daly Cherry-Evans kicked the crucial drop goal as the Sydney Roosters held on by one point to break Newcastle Knights hearts in a dramatic NRL Grand Final.
metadata.content: NRL Grand Final: Daly Cherry-Evans kicks crucial drop goal as Sydney Roosters hold on by one point to break Newcastle Knights hearts | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NRL Grand Final: Daly Cherry-Evans kicks crucial drop goal as Sydney Roosters hold on by one point to break Newcastle Knights hearts Dual-code international winger Mark Nawaqanitawase scored two tries as the Sydney Roosters edged the Newcastle Knights ‌19-18 in the National Rugby League final on Sunday, securing the foundation club a 16th title Sunday 4 October 2026 12:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kalyn Ponga produced a moment of magic in the NRL Grand Final with this full field try! Hull FC-bound Daly Cherry-Evans kicked the crucial drop goal as the Sydney Roosters held on by one point to break Newcastle Knights hearts in a dramatic NRL Grand Final. The Roosters overturned a 12-point deficit to deny Newcastle a fairytale ending to their Cinderella season and claim a 16th premiership after a thrilling Grand Final in Sydney. Inspirational captain, James Tedesco, and a show-stopping performance from Mark Nawaqanitawase, who could represent Australia at ‌both the league and union World Cups over the next 12 months, handed the Red White and Bluesters their first title since 2019. metadata.summary: Max Verstappen overcame a chaotic, twice-delayed, rain-affected race to claim his first win of the 2026 season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli strengthened his title bid with second place as George Russell retired late on.
metadata.content: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen wins first race of 2026 F1 season in wild, rain-hit Grand Prix as Lewis Hamilton surges back | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen wins first race of 2026 F1 season in wild, rain-hit Grand Prix as Lewis Hamilton surges back Torrential rain, lengthy race-start delay, formation lap chaos, botched tyre gambles and Safety Cars contribute to a remarkable day at Sepang; Max Verstappen ends Red Bull's wait for another win; Kimi Antonelli's extends title lead to 84 points after engine fault forces George Russell out Sunday 4 October 2026 15:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit. Max Verstappen overcame a chaotic, twice-delayed, rain-affected race to claim his first win of the 2026 season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli strengthened his title bid with second place as George Russell retired late on. Formula 1's return to Sepang after a nine-year absence produced the most remarkable race day of the season, with heavy rain before the start finally delivering the campaign's first wet-weather action at its 16th round. The start time was twice pushed back by delays before the 55 laps were twice disrupted by Safety Cars. Verstappen beat Antonelli to victory, while Lewis Hamilton stunningly fought back from dropping to 18th after a Ferrari tyre-strategy gamble backfired
